newsitem.title: CHINA: HK'S TSANG SAYS THAI BAILOUT HELPS ASIA COOPERATION.
newsitem.headline: HK'S TSANG SAYS THAI BAILOUT HELPS ASIA COOPERATION.

text.p: The rescue package to bail out Thailand will help regional central banks work together in future, Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Monday.

"I'm quite sure that this package will enhance...cooperation among governors of central banks in Asia," Tsang told reporters, after announcing that Hong Kong will contribute US$1 billion to a US$16 billion rescue package for Thailand.
The package was organised by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which called a meeting of bankers in Tokyo, including the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).

In Tokyo, HKMA chief executive Joseph Yam said participants in the IMF meeting, saw it as "an historic crossroads in regional financial cooperation and possibly as a precursor of standing arrangements".
The US$16 billion facility "will be more than adequate" to help the baht, which has been hit by speculative selling pressure in recent months, Tsang said.
Thailand was the first victim of a wave of speculative selling that spread to other currencies in the region, including Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines and Singapore.
Tsang said the US$1 billion contribution from Hong Kong was interest-bearing and would be repaid in about five years.
While the Hong Kong dollar, which is pegged to the U.S. dollar, had been "extremely strong and robust" in recent attacks on Asian currencies, he felt a duty towards Thailand, he said.
"I do believe that as a regional financial centre we just cannot stand idly by," he said.
"And also, if there is any major contagion effect arising from speculative activities in neighbouring areas, Hong Kong might be affected as well," Tsang said.
Tsang said the package involved major reforms in Thailand.
"There will be radical changes to the monetary and banking system in Thailand, and it will then stabilise the (Thai) currency," he said.
He added: "We are committed to regional monetary stability."
The package includes contributions from Australia, Singapore and Malaysia, Indonesia, Korea, Japan and the IMF and China is considering joining the rescue.

Yam also said that Thai authorities had adopted a policy reform package, representing a determination by the Thai authorities "to steer the economy on the right track and restore the stability of the financial sector in Thailand."
"This will contribute to the overall financial stability of the region," Yam added.
